{{Short description|English academic}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2021}}
[[Reverend|The Rev.]] '''Richard Harington''' (5 May 1800 – 13 December 1853) was an [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] [[Colleges of the University of Oxford|college]] [[Chief executive officer|head]] in the 19th century.<ref>[http://www.victorianweb.org/art/stainedglass/brasenose/3.html Victorian Web]</ref>

He was born in [[Hanover Square, Westminster]] and educated at [[Brasenose College, Oxford]].<ref>{{alox2|title=Harington, Richard (2)}}</ref> A mathematician, he was Principal of Brasenose<ref>[https://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/about-brasenose/history/216-brasenose-people/413-principals-list-of-past-and-present BNC web-site]</ref> from 1842<ref>'University And Clerical Intelligence' [[The Times]] Monday, 13 June 1842 Issue 18008 p.6</ref> until his death.<ref>'Deaths' [[The Times]] Friday, 16 December 1853 Issue 21613 p.9</ref>

A son was [[Sir Richard Harington, 11th Baronet]].
